[182] National Security Strategy (document

[183] Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed and worsened the security situation in our part of the world

[184] The exercise of power through military force is once again a reality in Europe and our surrounding area

[185] It is clear that Russia does not respect the laws of war and that civilian infrastructure and the civilian population are seen as legitimate targets

[186] Russia has incurred extensive personnel and material losses in Ukraine, primarily within the army forces

[187] However, the building up of new Russian military capabilities and the recovery of capabilities lost in Ukraine is ongoing

[188] Russia's military capability in Sweden's vicinity with air and naval forces remains, as does the ability to operate with hybrid means and special forces

[189] China's deepening partnership with Russia and enabling Russia's offensive war

[190] against Ukraine contributes to the serious security situation in Europe

[191] In light of the deteriorating security situation, Sweden and Finland applied for NATO membership in May

[192] Since March 7, 2024, Sweden has been a member of the alliance

[193] The integration of Sweden into NATO's political and military structures has proceeded rapidly, but the work of fully incorporating Sweden into the alliance's plans and capabilities will need to continue in the coming period

[194] In light of the deteriorating international situation and as a new member of NATO, Sweden is facing an epoch-making total defense decision

[195] Since taking office in the fall of 2022, the government has made major investments in total defense

[196] The allocation for military defense has doubled since 2020 and investments in civil defense have multiplied since

[197] The reconstruction of the defense began in 2015, but is being done after a long period of shrinking resources, as the procurement of equipment and supplies, training and infrastructure have not been sized to meet the Prop

[198] threat picture that is today a reality and where the construction of civil defense has had to take a back seat

[199] To achieve a relevant ability, determination and perseverance will be required

[200] As described in the government's national security strategy (document 2023/24:163), the development of total defence should be given great importance when weighing up and prioritizing different societal interests

[201] NATO's collective defense commitments affect total defense qualitatively and quantitatively

[202] As an ally, Sweden is part of the alliance's overall deterrence and defense, including nuclear deterrence

[203] Key commitments are also to strengthen our national defense and to maintain and strengthen society's preparedness and resilience

[204] An initial priority for Sweden is joining NATO's integrated air and missile defense

[205] Other priorities include Sweden's participation in NATO's forward presence in Latvia, in NATO's standing naval forces, in NATO's airspace surveillance, and in the role as a framework nation for NATO's forward presence in Finland

[206] Measures must also be taken to increase Sweden's capacity for host country support, something that also largely encompasses the civilian parts of total defense

[207] With strengthened national resilience through civil planning, Sweden can contribute to supporting the implementation of the alliance's defense plans

[208] Sweden should be a credible and reliable ally that contributes in solidarity to the collective defense efforts within NATO

[209] This requires a strong capability within total defense

[210] The deteriorating security situation makes the complementary roles of the EU and NATO clear

[211] NATO plays a crucial role in deterrence, while the EU is responsible for significant political, economic, humanitarian, legal and military support to Ukraine as well as the sanctions policy against Russia and Belarus

[212] Within the EU, steps have also been taken to strengthen the overall European military capability development, as well as the defense industrial and technological base within the Union

[213] Against this background, the government proposes, in line with the Defence Committee's proposal, that significant funds be allocated to military and civilian defence to finance the proposals in this direction for total defence 2025–

[214] The additions that the government is proposing to military and civil defense will enable, for example, four brigades to be essentially operational by 2030, an expanded procurement of air defense and supplies, an expanded refresher training and important investments to increase the capabilities of civil defense in areas such as emergency services, electronic communications and electricity supply

[215] With an increased level of ambition and significant financial contributions, it is required that the funds provided are used effectively and lead to the intended effect

[216] The Government intends to review laws, regulations and working methods to remove obstacles to the development of total defence

[217] This may, for example, apply to different forms of licensing and other restrictions

[218] The management of defense also needs to be adapted to promote and accelerate growth within total defense

[219] The foundations of this adaptation are to delegate decision-making to the most appropriate level, to strengthen the government's follow-up and to improve the conditions for long-term planning

[220] Military defense The government's priority for the coming period is to quickly build military capability and achieve materially and personnel-fulfilled and jointly trained units that meet the requirements of global developments and Sweden's ambition to be a credible, reliable and supportive ally

[221] The build-up of military defense is urgent and the development of the war organization needs to be accelerated in relation to current plans

[222] In order to accelerate capability growth during the upcoming defense decision-making period, the government announces in the budget bill for 2025 contributions to military defense of over SEK 170 billion for the period 2025–2030, in accordance with the framework proposed by the Defense Committee

[223] The government estimates that defense spending, according to NATO accounting practices, will amount to 2.2 percent of GDP as early as

[224] With the additions made to finance the direction of military defense in 2025–2030, defense spending as a share of GDP is estimated to amount to around 2.6 percent in

[225] The present bill increases the pace of military unit production while at the same time increasing the utilization of military units

[226] Support for Ukraine has generated a need for re-acquisition of equipment and supplies

[227] Overall, the use of Swedish units has increased, resulting in increased wear and tear on equipment and infrastructure and increased maintenance costs

[228] This also greatly affects the working conditions of defence personnel

[229] In addition, over time, a need has accumulated for capability-enhancing measures within military defense of a more fundamental nature

[230] The overall development of military defense in the coming years

[231] will largely be qualitative rather than quantitative in terms of the number of combat units

[232] During the period, the government proposes that a significant portion of defense appropriations be spent on renovating, modifying and extending the service life of existing equipment and on procuring new supplies such as ammunition

[233] Personnel in various categories also need to be recruited and trained, and the number of conscripts needs to increase

[234] The Armed Forces need to be an attractive employer in order to recruit and retain personnel

[235] Linked to this, the government in the bill makes a special investment in infrastructure that has long been neglected, also with regard to the war organization

[236] In accordance with the Defence Committee's proposal, the government is prioritizing the development of four brigades by 2030 and the conditions required to achieve this

[237] The government's priorities for the navy and air force also follow the Defence Committee's proposals

[238] Special funds are allocated to increase personnel in the navy

[239] Special attention is given to the training of officers and conscripts, including refresher training

[240] It is proposed to increase the volume of basic training for conscripts and refresher training

[241] The war in Ukraine demonstrates the importance of functioning air defense and long-range combat capability, the central role of drones in the theater of war, and how important parts of the war are taking place in the cyber domain

[242] In light of these experiences and the Defence Committee's reports, the Government proposes an expansion of air defence capabilities within various parts of the war organisation, a commencement of development of Prop

[243] rocket artillery capabilities, acquisition of autonomous and unmanned vehicles and strengthening the ability for defensive and offensive cyber operations

[244] Experiences from the war in Ukraine also strengthen the understanding of the close connection between materiel issues, defense innovation, research and development

[245] New equipment systems must be delivered faster and within the specified time frame

[246] Security of supply needs to increase

[247] The Government therefore proposes that investments in research and development be strengthened so that new capabilities can be developed and self-sufficiency ensured in integrity-critical areas

[248] The exchange between the civilian and military sectors within industry, academia and government agencies needs to continue to develop

[249] The importance of being able to interpret, structure and predict one's environment has also been made clear on the modern battlefield

[250] The Government therefore proposes that the defence intelligence capability and the military security service continue to be developed and that national and international cooperation be deepened

[251] The total defense bill also enables the acquisition of reconnaissance and surveillance satellites, which is an important step in developing Swedish space capabilities and part of the government's defense and security strategy for space

[252] Within the framework of digitalization of functions within military defense, the government proposes measures that are, among other things, necessary to be able to utilize advanced operational systems and conduct multi-domain operations

[253] NATO membership places increased demands on interoperability with NATO allies

[254] The government therefore proposes that the war organization be expanded in certain areas within command and logistics and that a new category of units intended for territorial tasks be introduced

[255] The government's priority for the coming period is to continue strengthening the capacity within civil defense and to increase the pace of development

[256] Civil defense should be built based on the requirements set in high alert and extreme war and have the ability to contribute to the capabilities of military defense, ensure the most important societal functions and protect the civilian population

[257] Civil defense must also have the ability to maintain the will to defend and society's resilience to external pressures

[258] Russia's brutal warfare in Ukraine illustrates the devastation and strain that Sweden and its allies may face

[259] Sweden's civil defense needs to be built based on the requirements set in high alert and extreme war

[260] Actors in society must take measures to be able to meet and handle an armed attack

[261] According to the government, a war requires that decision-makers in both public and private sectors have an approach and a culture that can handle the consequences that an armed attack can bring

[262] The government is introducing an economic planning framework for civil defense with the aim of preparing Sweden for heightened preparedness and, in the event of war

[263] A financial planning framework creates predictability, long-term planning and transparency in the direction of civil defense, as well as an increased opportunity to prioritize and follow up on the results of the measures taken

[264] Based on the financial planning framework for civil defense, the government therefore intends to strengthen governance and follow-up in the area

[265] The development of civil defense is taking place from a very low level and the pace of development needs to increase urgently and be based on the demands made in a state of heightened alert and, in the extreme, war

[266] The measures that quickly produce the greatest effect and thereby increase capacity within the most important societal functions should be prioritized

[267] The goal of capability development should be a civil defense that is resilient to societal disruption and can handle the consequences of an armed attack

[268] Such civil defense contributes to strengthening society's ability to prevent and manage peacetime crisis situations

[269] The management of civil defense in high alert and extreme war situations should be carried out by actors with geographical area responsibility

[270] In times of heightened alert and extreme war, it is necessary that decisions at different levels can be made independently for the highest possible defense effect

[271] This requires that responsibilities and mandates are clearly allocated to relevant levels

[272] The roles and mandates of county administrative boards responsible for civil areas and sector-responsible authorities need to be strengthened

[273] A fundamental task of civil defense is to protect the civilian population

[274] Experience from Ukraine shows that it is particularly important to strengthen the emergency services and that initiatives already underway in these areas continue to be strengthened

[275] A functioning civil protection system also contributes to maintaining the population's will to defend itself and resilience

[276] The government reports on a series of measures within civil protection

[277] The functionality of the social economy is of paramount importance for total defense and for maintaining the capability of the most important societal functions

[278] The government proposes investments in all broad sectors

[279] In addition to investments in emergency services and protection of the civilian population, priority is also given to measures in electronic communications and mail, energy supply and transport, as well as food supply and drinking water

[280] The government continues to provide funds that, together with previous investments, strengthen civil defense in health, care and welfare. Sweden's economic resilience needs to be strengthened

[281] A functioning business sector, trade with the outside world and financial stability are fundamental factors for maintaining society's functionality at the highest possible level

[282] It is necessary to develop a structure where Sweden's needs for essential goods and services can be identified

[283] For a credible total defense, all activities within civil defense need to have good basic information and cyber security

[284] Critical operations need to be able to withstand cyber attacks, and information and cyber security must therefore be prioritized, not least at management level

[285] Psychological defense is also an important component

[286] In order to safeguard and strengthen the will to defend, the population's resilience and self-preparedness, the ability to prevent, identify, analyse and respond to undue information influence and to ensure the transmission of information even under disturbed conditions needs to continue to be developed. The resilience of society is part of NATO's collective deterrence and defence

[287] Sweden's efforts to develop and strengthen civil defense

[288] and total defense planning is thus an important contribution to the alliance's deterrence and defense

[289] In times of heightened alert and extreme war, civil defense activities should in every situation be focused on supporting military defense in the manner that is most appropriate to support the overall war effort of the total defense

[290] In parallel with the government's major investments in total defense, substantial political, economic, humanitarian, civilian and military support continues

[291] to Ukraine to be implemented

[292] The military support packages that have been donated have included army equipment of various types but also air defense equipment, ammunition and maintenance solutions

[293] This includes training of Ukrainian personnel and financial support

[294] Civilian support includes, for example, donations of jet skis, medical supplies, fire protection, generators and tents

[295] The government's three-year framework for military support totaling SEK 75 billion, divided into SEK 25 billion annually from 2024 to 2026, clarifies Sweden's long-term commitment to support Ukraine

[296] It contributes to predictability and efficiency and is an important political signal to the outside world

[297] Decisions on the detailed content of the support will be made on an ongoing basis. Sweden's support to Ukraine is sustainable and long-term and also includes reconstruction

[298] The government is presenting the Total Defence Bill at a time of major changes in the world

[299] The bill is being presented during a raging war in Europe, the outcome of which will affect the security situation in our immediate area and globally for the foreseeable future

[300] This means that Europe will have to take greater responsibility for its security

[301] Sweden also makes its total defense decision

[302] during a formative period for NATO

[303] During the period Sweden is included

[304] fully in NATO's regional planning with the operational consequences

[305] this may mean

[306] On July 1, 2024, NATO presented drafts of the alliance's new overall capability goals, called capability targets

[307] The draft capability goals represent a significant increase in the ambition of military capabilities within the alliance

[308] The goals will be decided in October

[309] Overall, the implementation of the defense decision will take place during a time characterized by significant uncertainty

[310] Developments in the outside world will have a central impact, where the total defense authorities will need to balance sharp operations and international cooperation against their own growth

[311] Added to this are uncertainties in the supply of defense equipment, in a situation where the defense industry in Europe and the United States is facing a demand that is many times greater than supply

[312] In this external and market situation, the Government believes that it is justified to adapt government management based on the need for rapid growth and to be prepared to adjust the direction based on external developments

[313] Swedish NATO membership and other external factors that affect the implementation of the defense decision

[314] Security policy 4.1 Overall security policy development The Government's assessment

[315] The world is in a time of transition

[316] Today's rules-based world order is being challenged by authoritarian states

[317] Security policy developments are characterized by an intensifying geopolitical power struggle that encompasses more and more areas of society

[318] States use a wide range of tools to achieve their security policy objectives

[319] The security situation in Sweden's immediate vicinity and globally is characterized by instability and unpredictability

[320] Because of Russia, a large-scale war is raging in Europe

[321] The effects of the war are not limited to Ukraine

[322] Therefore, the conditions for Swedish security policy have fundamentally changed

[323] Since March 7, 2024, Sweden has been a member of NATO

[324] Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine shows that conflicts over territory using military means are once again a reality

[325] China's strategic and military actions are increasingly affecting security in the Euro-Atlantic area, including Sweden's immediate vicinity

[326] An armed attack against Sweden or our allies cannot be ruled out

[327] It cannot be ruled out that military force or threats of such might be used against Sweden or our allies

[328] There is a broad and increasingly complex threat picture against Sweden and Swedish interests, as well as increased risks to Swedish security

[329] The threats include, among other things, undue influence on information, cyberattacks, illegal intelligence gathering, terrorism and sabotage, threats against socially important activities and exploitation of economic dependencies

[330] Foreign powers, terrorists and violent extremists act in a way that means that the threats overlap and are amplified

[331] Cyberattacks from state and other actors are constantly ongoing against Swedish interests, and Sweden has been and continues to be the subject of security-threatening activities from foreign powers

[332] Overall, the threat to Sweden has increased, while Sweden is given opportunities for collective defense as a NATO ally

[333] The reasons for the government's assessment

[334] In the following section, the Government presents the basis for its assessment regarding global trends, the rules-based world order and Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine

[335] Global trends

[336] The world is in a time of transition

[337] Today's rules-based world order, with the UN Charter as its foundation, was established after the Second World War and developed after the end of the Cold War

[338] It is now being challenged by authoritarian Prop

[339] states

[340] It is fundamentally a conflict between democratic states that want to maintain the rules-based order and authoritarian and revisionist states that believe they have the right to their own spheres of interest where they have decisive influence over neighboring states

[341] Russia's aggression against Ukraine since 2014, including the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, violates international law, including the UN Charter's prohibition of violence, and the European security order, including the norms, cooperation and institutions that form the foundation of European security

[342] Despite its commitments to comply with the agreed rules, Russia has repeatedly and flagrantly violated international law

[343] Russia's great power ambitions, military buildup and claims to determine the political choices of other states undermine security in Russia's immediate vicinity, Europe and globally

[344] Russia's war against Ukraine is both an attack on Ukraine and part of an overall systemic conflict with the West

[345] China pursues an increasingly system-revisionist foreign policy and a repressive domestic policy

[346] This ultimately aims to preserve the Communist Party's hold on power

[347] By redefining concepts such as democracy and human rights, it attempts to

[349] China is carrying out a comprehensive military buildup and modernization

[351] The Chinese leadership's ambition is for the country to be one of the world's leading military powers by

[353] The intensifying geopolitical power struggle is affecting more and more areas of society

[354] States use a wide range of tools to achieve their security policy objectives, which makes it more difficult to assess what constitutes a threat

[355] Authoritarian states like Russia and China use the full breadth of their societies' resources to advance their interests

[356] The geopolitical contradictions also make it more difficult to deal with crossborder threats such as climate change, pandemics, attacks on strategic infrastructure, terrorism, violent extremism and organized crime

[357] The increasing geopolitical power struggle is also taking place in Sweden's immediate vicinity

[358] In parallel, there is a global decline in democracy as a form of government and a lack of respect for human rights, gender equality and the principles of the rule of law

[359] Over the past decade, countries in several regions, including within Europe, have developed in an authoritarian direction

[362] Globally, there is a growing contradiction between democratic states on the one hand and authoritarian and system revisionist states on the other

[363] For a number of years, there has been an economic, political and military shift in the center of gravity from Western Europe and North America to Asia

[376] Digitalization and the information society

[377] Digital development brings great benefits to society, but also increases existing threats and creates new ones

[378] Digitalization leads to complex chains of dependency where the weaknesses of an individual actor can pose a risk to other actors

[379] Digitalization has made the cyber area a prominent domain for threats and attacks, e.g. targeting public institutions, companies and financial systems that have critical societal functions

[380] Even seemingly limited attacks can cause difficulties and create concern among the population

[381] Digital robustness across the entire conflict scale is therefore of great importance

[384] Technological developments bring about continuous change in society and the military operational environment

[385] Developments in areas such as information technology, artificial intelligence (AI), sensors, robotics, materials technology, biotechnology, energy technology and quantum technology can lead to significant changes with far-reaching economic, political and military consequences

[398] The dependence on undersea cables and pipelines for telecommunications and energy transmission constitutes an example of a critical vulnerability that could be affected

[399] These vulnerabilities allow antagonistic measures to be used in an increasing number of arenas and often regardless of distance

[400] At the same time, it is difficult to identify the attacker, which makes deterrence and countermeasures more difficult

[401] Overall, it is difficult to draw a line between internal and external security and between military and non-military threats

[402] Often it can be a combination of different activities

[404] This form of antagonistic action is usually described as a hybrid threat

[405] The activities may be part of war preparations, but are carried out to a significantly greater extent at a low intensity in peacetime and are therefore something that society must be able to handle even without special decisions on heightened preparedness and with both civilian and military means

[406] The threats require capabilities that partly fall outside the structure and task of total defence

[407] Managing threats requires improved situational awareness as well as leadership and decision-making skills

[408] It also requires improved collaboration between different sectors and decision-making levels in society, between the public and private sectors, and developed international collaborations

[409] The Government intends to strengthen the ability to identify, manage and respond to hybrid threats and attacks

[410] The work of reducing vulnerabilities and strengthening resilience in society is an important part of this

[411] The attacker's goal is to advance their interests

[412] The purpose can also be to test, practice or demonstrate certain abilities

[413] The approach is Prop. 2024/25:34 has existed at all times

[415] Russia makes extensive use of various types of antagonistic actions that can be used instead of, in combination with, or in preparation for military force

[416] An armed attack may be preceded by an attacker carrying out escalated active, often subversive, hybrid activities for a shorter or longer period of time without triggering a state of war

[417] Deception is an important instrument even in peacetime hybrid operations

[441] Unless strong measures are taken to rapidly reduce global greenhouse gas emissions, the 1.5 degree target will not be achieved, which will have major consequences

[444] Sea level rise may eventually threaten parts of countries' territories and, in some cases, their very existence, leading to conflicts over maritime borders

[452] The rules-based world order

[453] The rules-based world order is under pressure

[454] Several states, both regionally and globally, are trying to challenge international rules and norms

[455] Multilateral cooperation and institutions are increasingly being undermined

[456] The driving force in advocating for a different order is Russia and China

[457] The countries are working towards what they call a multipolar world order consisting of several different centers of power and values, and have the ambition to weaken the position of the United States and the rest of the Western world globally

[458] They also show a lack of respect for human rights

[459] Maintaining the rules-based world order and respect for international law constitute central and long-term foreign and security policy interests for Sweden

[460] The alternative would be a world ruled by great powers where the territorial integrity and sovereignty of smaller states, including the right to choose their own security policies, are not respected

[461] The rules-based world order is based on international law, including the UN Charter, and consists of rules and principles that define the boundaries of what constitutes legitimate and acceptable behavior between states

[462] The European security order refers to the set of rules and principles, binding under international law as well as politically binding, which together form the foundation for Europe's security and thus its prosperity

[463] These include rules prohibiting the threat or use of force, regardless of whether it is directed against the territorial integrity or political independence of another state, as well as respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity and right of each state to independently and without interference determine its security policy path

[464] The European security order is based on the UN Charter and further developed in the Helsinki Final Act of 1975 and the Charter of Paris of 1990, together with the other political commitments negotiated within the framework of the Conference on European Security, later the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE

[465] for Russian crimes is important for redress and justice for Ukraine as a state and for the people who fall victim to Russia's aggression and other violations of international law, but also for the maintenance of the rules-based world order

[467] The view on Russia's violations of international law and threats to the European security order is almost unanimous within the EU, NATO, the G7 (France, Italy, Japan, Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany and the United States) and broader Western cooperation

[468] A large majority of countries in the UN General Assembly have strongly condemned

[469] Overall, there is therefore strong international support for the UN Charter, international law and the rules-based world order

Security policy developments in certain regions The security situation both in Sweden's immediate vicinity and globally is characterized by instability and unpredictability

[483] Developments in the immediate area, not least after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, as well as developments in Asia, especially China's increasingly confrontational stance and strength, are having an increasing impact on Swedish security and defense policy

[484] The Government shares the assessment made by the Defence Committee, namely that the seriousness of the general security policy situation has become even more acute

[485] At the same time, it is the government's assessment that Sweden's and Finland's membership in NATO has contributed to improving the security situation for Sweden and our neighboring countries

[486] The assessment of the security policy situation is fraught with a number of uncertainties, not least with regard to the continued development of Russia's war in Ukraine, Russia's confrontational stance towards the EU, NATO and its member states, developments in the Middle East, tensions in the Indo-Pacific region and political developments in a number of countries important to Sweden

[487] These uncertainty factors, individually or collectively, entail an increased risk that the security situation could rapidly deteriorate further, with serious consequences for the security of Europe and Sweden

[598] Russia has the world's largest and most diversified nuclear weapons arsenal at both the intercontinental and sub-regional levels

[1332] The total defense is designed and dimensioned to defend Sweden against an armed attack and contribute to the defense of allies in accordance with the commitments that follow from membership in NATO

[1333] This includes planning to respond to acts of war on Swedish territory as well as on allied territory

[1334] The combined capabilities of the Swedish total defense system thus form part of the collective defense within NATO

[1335] The endurance of total defense should create freedom of action to adjust society for a longer period of serious security crisis or war

[1336] A strong Swedish total defense that contributes to NATO's collective deterrence is war-repelling and thus conflict-preventing and ultimately peace-preserving

[1337] The reasons for the government's assessment

[1338] Total defense is the type of activity needed to prepare Sweden for war

[1339] Total defense consists of military activities (military defense) and civilian activities (civil defense

[1340] During the highest state of alert, total defense is all societal activities that must be conducted at that time

[1341] Military and civil defense are mutually reinforcing

[1342] As a member of NATO, Sweden is covered by the defense commitments that follow from the North Atlantic Treaty and NATO's conventional and nuclear deterrence capabilities

[1343] NATO membership increases Sweden's defense capabilities by providing greater opportunities to cooperate with allies across the full spectrum of conflicts. Sweden's total defense is designed and dimensioned to defend the country against armed attack and contribute to the defense of allies

[1344] This includes planning to respond to acts of war on Swedish territory but also for the participation of Swedish units in operations on allied territory according to the planning within NATO

[1345] The ability to participate in and support NATO military operations according to NATO operational plans needs to be developed in close cooperation with NATO and our neighboring countries, especially Norway, Finland and Denmark, and with other troop-contributing allies

[1346] This will require, among other things, coherent management and logistics

[1347] Civil defense will have important tasks in supporting military operations

[1348] The endurance of total defense should create freedom of action to adjust society for a longer period of serious security crisis or war

[1349] This means, among other things, that important parts of the Swedish economy can be maintained, that military support to and from allies can be ensured, that civilian support from allies and the EU can be enabled, and that joint NATO operations that include Swedish territory can be carried out

[1350] The Defence Committee (Ds 2023:34) states that in the event of a threat of war or war, the efforts of the total defence will be concentrated on military defence and that society will need to adjust to war conditions

[1351] The military and civilian defense, within the framework of a cohesive total defense, must prepare and plan to be able to face and manage a war in Europe for at least three months that leads to serious consequences for the functionality of society

[1352] The Defence Committee assesses that the three months give society time to adjust to wartime conditions, with, for example, changed production conditions and flows of goods, and thus to be able to manage a longer period of serious security crisis or war

[1353] The Defence Committee further believes that normal functionality in society should be maintained as far as possible even in war

[1354] However, the committee emphasizes that the ambition of peacetime total defense preparations should be to maintain the most important societal functions during war

[1355] This means a significantly lower ambition in most sectors of society compared to the normal situation

[1356] It also means major limitations and a great effort across society and from all residents to cope with such a situation

[1357] The Government does not make any different assessment than the Defence Committee regarding what has been said above regarding planning conditions, etc

[1358] At the same time, the government notes that the time for transition to wartime conditions is likely to vary within different preparedness sectors and within different parts of the business community

[1359] The Government will return to issues relating to civil defence in Chapter 7, where this is further developed

[1360] Total defense is a matter for the entire society

[1361] The individual's own responsibility constitutes an important part of society's overall ability to resist and alleviate the consequences of the serious disruptions in society's

[1362] functionality that a war can bring

[1364] However, this internal preparedness needs to be strengthened

[1366] The Defence Committee notes that the public's knowledge and ability to prepare for emergencies will have a major impact on both the burden on the public sector and the overall resilience of society

[1367] The ability to withstand serious disruptions to the functionality of society in war is central to the ability of total defence to make an effective contribution to NATO's overall deterrence capability. Overall goals for total defence The government's proposal

[1368] The overall goal of total defense should be to have the ability to defend Sweden and our population against armed attack, assert our country's independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity, and contribute to the defense of allies

[1369] Activities within total defence should be able to be conducted individually and together with others, within and outside the country and in accordance with Sweden's commitments as a member of NATO

[1370] The reasons for the government's proposal

[1371] The Government proposes the same overall goals for total defence as the Defence Committee

[1372] The Defence Committee believes that the government's vital security interests (see section 4.5.4 Security policy orientation) and membership in NATO should be reflected in the overall goal of total defence

[1373] Through the 2020 Defense Decision (Government Bill No

[1374] Through the 2020 Defense Decision an overall goal for total defense was introduced

[1375] The purpose of the goal is

[1376] to achieve a combined capability in total defence through common starting points and a common objective and focus. The Government believes that military and civilian defence need to continue to develop in a coordinated manner and that coherent planning for total defence is needed

[1382] Through NATO membership, Sweden undertakes, in accordance with Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, to provide support without delay in the event of an armed attack against any of NATO's member states

[1383] NATO membership also means that our national defence capability forms part of the Alliance's collective defence, in accordance with Article 3 of the North Atlantic Treaty, which states that the Member States shall, individually and together, through their own preparedness and mutual assistance, maintain and develop their individual and collective ability to resist armed attack. The development of Sweden's total defence thus also contributes to the development of collective defence capabilities within the Alliance. Military measures to defend Sweden and our population and the territory of allies must be complemented by civilian measures and preparations for strengthened national resilience by increasing the resilience of society and the preparedness of civilian actors

[1385] Goals for military defense. The government's proposal

[1386] The goal of military defense shall be to have the ability to – defend Sweden against armed attack, – assert Sweden's territorial integrity, – safeguard rights and national interests outside Swedish territory in accordance with international law, – within the framework of NATO's collective defense and other tasks, fulfill Sweden's commitments as a member of NATO, – promote our security and prevent and manage conflicts and wars by carrying out operations on our own territory and in the surrounding area in peacetime and participating in international peace-promoting efforts, – protect society and its functionality by using existing capabilities and resources to assist the rest of society both in peacetime and at times of heightened alert

[1419] Goals for civil defense

[1420] The goal of civil defence shall be to have the ability to – ensure the most important societal functions, – within the framework of NATO's collective defence and other tasks, contribute to the capability of military defence, – protect the civilian population, – maintain the will to defend and society's resilience to external pressures

[1618] The Defence Committee's view

[1619] Ukrainian experiences regarding warfare point to, among other things, the importance of various forms of air defense in order to be able to defend against long-range missile defense, air strikes and drone attacks

[1620] The components of the national air defense should, in addition to fighter and reconnaissance aircraft, consist of sensors as well as kinetic attack systems and electronic warfare attack systems

[1621] Another area of ​​great importance is the cyber domain

[1622] Before and in the initial phases of the full-scale invasion, a number of Russian cyberattacks were carried out, which were, however, in several cases countered by Ukrainian measures

[1623] Operations in the cyber domain have become an integral part of warfare during the ongoing invasion, where, for example, cyberattacks, remote combat and influence operations have been combined to achieve the desired effect

[1624] Experience from warfare shows that long-range combat capability in the land, sea and air domains is important for creating the conditions for one's own mobility and for enabling combat against the enemy's troop concentrations and supply lines

[1625] Unmanned vehicles in the air and sea domains have proven to have great effect both within the framework of reconnaissance and combat

[1626] These unmanned systems are in some cases to be considered as ammunition rather than as exclusive action or sensor systems, which means that large volumes are required to achieve sufficient endurance

[1627] Areas such as command, logistics, indirect fire and field operations have in several respects once again demonstrated their great importance for the conduct of the battle, as has the use of different types of units where the level of equipment and technology is adapted based on varying tactical and combat economic conditions

[1628] This applies, for example, to maneuver units versus units for more stationary tasks or different types of air defense units

[1629] The warfare in Ukraine also shows the enormous consumption of supplies, including ammunition, that a large-scale war entails

[1630] The war's extension in time and space has also meant that quantitative aspects of warfare have become relevant in a way that has not characterized the design of Western defense forces for a long time, nor has it characterized the Swedish one

[1631] This applies, for example, to the number of units of various types, the need to be able to mobilize and produce combat units during an ongoing war, the care of the wounded and fallen on a larger scale, and the ability to continuously repair and, if necessary, modify equipment, even under field conditions

[1632] Based on the geographical and other conditions prevailing in the context, the war has highlighted the central importance of the land domain for the course of battle. Regarding innovation and technological development, the war in Ukraine has shown that there is a need to create conditions for adapting one's own sensors and weapons systems to the dynamic development that a war has, as this is crucial if tactical development is to be possible

[1633] To achieve success in this area, systems need to be created in collaboration with the defense industry and authorities already in peacetime

[1634] The importance of stockpiling raw materials and equipment with long delivery or production times is also an important experience from Ukraine

[1635] The Government believes that lessons learned from the war in Ukraine should be continuously analyzed and taken into account in the development of Swedish total defense

[1636] At the same time, it needs to be taken into account that certain observed experiences may be unique in terms of time and space and thus less relevant for future warfare

Society's resilience is part of NATO's collective deterrence and defence According to Article 3 of the North Atlantic Treaty, NATO Allies shall individually and together maintain and develop their individual and collective capacity to resist armed attack

[2519] is the foundation for NATO's work to strengthen the alliance's resilience by increasing societal resilience and the preparedness of civilian actors

[2520] In the NATO context, the work on strengthening resilience is about the Allies increasing their ability to prepare for, withstand, respond to and quickly recover from crises arising from threats and risks aimed at the security of the Alliance

[2521] In NATO's strategic concept

[2522] From 2022, it is stated that maintaining and strengthening society's resilience is both a national responsibility and a collective commitment

[2523] Maintaining and strengthening societal resilience is essential for the credibility of the alliance's overall capability for both deterrence and defense

[2524] NATO's work on resilience and civilian preparedness is focused on three core tasks: the ability to maintain political decision-making and central command functions, the safeguarding of essential societal functions, and civilian support to military operations

[2525] Within the framework of the three core tasks, seven basic civilian capability requirements (baseline requirements for resilience) have been identified, against which Allies can measure their efforts: 1) ensuring political decision-making and

[2526] central management functions, 2) resilient energy supply, 3) effective management of uncontrolled population movements, 4) resilient food and drinking water supply systems, 5) management of mass casualty outcomes, 6) resilient civil communication systems, and 7) resilient transport systems

[2527] NATO's heads of state and government have agreed to develop overall resilience goals for the alliance that can be used in the allies' national development efforts

[2528] In connection with the NATO summit in Washington in 2024, the Allies also agreed to continue working on strengthened national resilience through civil planning to support the implementation of NATO's defense plans. Sweden's efforts to develop and strengthen civil defense and total defense planning are an important contribution to the Alliance's deterrence and defense

[2529] NATO and the allies' experiences of work in the area of ​​resilience, including the seven civilian capability requirements, are also important contributions to the national work of developing Sweden's crisis preparedness and civil defense

[2530] Create conditions for strengthened civil defence. Management structure and organisation of civil defence The Government's assessment

[2531] The management of civil defense in high alert and extreme war situations should be carried out by actors with geographical area responsibility

[2538] During periods of heightened alert and extreme war, activities consist of necessary measures to maintain the goal of civil defense

[2539] In the event of a heightened state of readiness, high demands are placed on the management and coordination of civil defence. [2736] According to the Defence Committee, a robust and cohesive economic defence needs to encompass both public activities at national, regional and local levels as well as the business sector

[2740] Therefore, it is also important that there is resilience in production and flow chains for trade and transport and supply chains, an ability within the business community to adjust production in the event of disrupted conditions and war or the threat of war, but also to ensure that there are stocks of necessary goods, including input goods such as minerals and metals

[2741] Supply readiness. The ability to ensure the most important societal functions is dependent on access to necessary goods and services, the ability to maintain or adjust production, and the protection and distribution of necessary goods and services

[2828] Ensure the capability in the most important societal functions within civil defense. The Government's assessment

[2829] Based on the serious security policy situation, the measures that quickly produce the greatest effect and thereby increase capacity within the most important societal functions need to be prioritized

[2830] In parallel, planning needs to take place that means that increased ability is also developed in the longer term

[2831] The reasons for the government's assessment

[2832] Since October 1, 2022, Sweden has had a new preparedness structure for civil defense and crisis preparedness

[2833] According to the Ordinance (2022:524) on the preparedness of government agencies, each agency must take into account the requirements of total defense in its operations

[2834] This includes planning so that the authority, in the event of a heightened state of alert, will continue its operations as far as possible, taking into account the availability of personnel and other conditions

[2835] The regulation further states that certain authorities are emergency response authorities and that most of these are divided into a number of different emergency response sectors

[2836] Emergency response authorities must have a good ability to resist threats and risks, prevent vulnerabilities and carry out their tasks during periods of heightened alert

[2837] In the event of a heightened state of alert and extreme war, the emergency response authorities shall primarily focus their activities on tasks that are important for total defense

[2838] The authority responsible for the sector shall, within its sector, lead the work of coordinating measures prior to and during a heightened state of readiness, and during a heightened state of readiness, based on need, provide the government with information regarding prioritization and distribution of resources within the preparedness sector

[2839] According to the government, it is particularly important that the emergency response authorities can maintain their operations in a situation of heightened alert and, in the extreme, war, as it is crucial for them to be able to contribute to the goal of civil defense and thus the goal of total defense

[2840] The capacity of civil defense needs to be strengthened when it comes to coping with both a sudden armed attack and a protracted conflict

[2841] Different parts of the preparedness structure have come to different lengths in their work to build the ability to maintain their operations at high alert

[2842] According to the government, it is now of utmost importance that the actors who have begun such work continue to develop their capabilities

[2843] Those government agencies that have not yet initiated such work should urgently begin doing so

[2844] Current regulations provide opportunities to act and take measures for increased preparedness, for example in terms of being able to maintain one's own vital operations and to work to ensure that other actors within the area of responsibility also carry out such work

[2845] In the following section, the Government explains the urgent needs that exist, among other things, in the preparedness sectors and where measures need to be taken during the defense decision period

[2846] Based on this, in combination with the funds proposed in the budget bill for 2025, the Government intends to create the conditions for civil defense actors to take capability-enhancing measures at a faster pace in order to achieve an increased ability to adapt their operations to a situation of heightened preparedness and, ultimately, war

[2847] Supply of critical goods and services and foreign trade

[2848] As part of achieving the goal of civil defense, the necessary supply of critical goods and services for the needs of total defense and foreign trade needs to be maintained during peacetime crises, heightened alert and, in the extreme, war

[2849] Therefore, the responsibilities of government agencies in these areas should be clarified in the current emergency preparedness and civil defense structure

[2850] The reasons for the government's assessment

[2851] The Government, like the Defence Committee, notes that the capability of total defence is directly linked to a functioning national economy

[2852] Furthermore, the Government shares the view that, in the event of a heightened state of alert, Sweden must be able to ensure the total defence's needs for goods and services and be able to maintain trade with the outside world

[2853] The Defence Committee notes that experience from Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine shows that the flow of goods and services is important for maintaining society's resilience and the country's economy

[2854] During the COVID-19 pandemic, it also became clear that complex supply chains posed particular problems around both deliveries and production

[2855] Sweden is dependent on both exports and imports of goods and services functioning in order to maintain a supply of critical goods and services

[2856] Trade in the EU's internal market and with third countries needs to be maintained even under disrupted conditions

[2857] In the event of war and the threat of war or under disturbed conditions, trade flows need to be ensured and the production capacity of critical goods and services that are important for activities within total defence needs to be ensured and maintained

[2858] As the Defence Committee notes, there are currently no designated emergency authorities responsible for maintaining trade with the outside world

[2859] There is also a lack of designated responsibility for ensuring the industry's supply of raw materials, etc., which is of central importance for maintaining the production of critical goods and services

[2860] The Defence Preparation Committee proposes that the coordination of measures relating to foreign trade and the supply of industrial goods in preparation for peacetime crisis situations and heightened preparedness should be organised into two new preparedness sectors: one for foreign trade and one for the supply of industrial goods

[2861] In March 2024, the government received the interim report

[2862] A new preparedness sector – for increased security of supply

[2863] In the interim report, the inquiry proposes that a preparedness sector should be established with responsibility for industry, construction and trade in order to maintain a necessary supply of goods and services in the event of a peacetime crisis, heightened alert or war

[2864] In addition, the investigation notes that several authorities that are central to Swedish security of supply are not included in any sector of the emergency preparedness system

[2865] The Defence Committee's assessment is that responsibility for maintaining the necessary supply of critical goods and services as well as foreign trade needs to be clarified in the current emergency preparedness structure for crisis preparedness and civil defence

[2866] The Government intends to clarify the responsibilities of government agencies in these areas

[2867] Financial security

[2868] The authorities within the economic security preparedness sector are responsible, among other things, for investigating, determining and paying government compensation and certain government salaries, as well as ensuring the basic financing of public activities

[2869] Determining and collecting taxes and fees is central to the national economy both during peacetime and during times of heightened alert and, in extreme cases, war

[2870] Operations in the emergency preparedness sector are mainly conducted within the public sector, with the exception of unemployment funds, which are economic associations

[2871] The authorities in the sector have a high degree of critical dependencies both within the sector and to activities where responsibility rests with actors in other sectors

[2872] This applies in particular to the supply of electricity, electronic communications, basic data, and functioning financial services

[2873] Issues regarding the payment system in general, cash management, electricity supply, IT supply, and information and cybersecurity are therefore absolutely central to maintaining the sector's operations

[2874] Within the sector there are also strong dependencies on the private sector, such as banks and insurance companies

[2875] Civil defense needs to be strengthened and developed to contribute to a higher overall capability within total defense

[2876] Government payments and determining and collecting taxes constitute essential activities that must always be maintained, even in the event of heightened alert and, in the extreme, war

[2877] The work in the sector is strengthened by allocating funds to emergency response authorities to develop work on civil defense and to increase resilience in secure IT systems

[2878] Strengthening robustness in payments and government payroll services requires active work to ensure a high level of information and cybersecurity in the operations included in the sector

[2879] A digital infrastructure that can withstand stress and meet high demands for operational reliability and robustness is essential for emergency authorities in the sector to be able to pay compensation and benefits

[2880] The Swedish Social Insurance Agency's operations depend on secure IT operations

[2881] A prerequisite for secure IT operations is protected IT spaces

[2882] The Government believes that it is important to achieve a stronger and more cohesive government IT operation (see also section

[2891] Electronic communications and mail

[2892] Virtually all sectors of society are characterized by increased digitalization and interconnection of information systems and infrastructure

[2893] In order for the total defense to be able to handle the consequences of an armed attack, maintaining electronic communications and mail is of great importance for both the Armed Forces and for actors in all preparedness sectors

[2894] For the Armed Forces, for example, it is important that orders for war deployment and military service can be distributed both electronically and physically in a very short time during high alert

[2895] For most businesses, there are currently no realistic alternatives to using electronic communications and digital services

[2896] Digitalization entails complex chains of dependency and needs to go hand in hand with increased information and cybersecurity

[2897] Significant threats to the infrastructure in the electronic communications and postal sector consist of both stresses in the cyber domain and physical attacks, such as sabotage or other external influences

[2898] Within the sector, there are emergency authorities responsible for secure and efficient electronic means of communication as well as a well-functioning postal service

[2899] The sector also includes emergency response authorities with extensive digital communications networks that are important for the functionality of society

[2900] These include infrastructure in all domains

[2901] In addition to these emergency response authorities, there are a large number of private companies that own, provide and operate to maintain the digital infrastructure that is very important to society in general and the national defense in particular

[2902] The area is complex, which places great demands on coordination, planning and management by the sector-responsible authority

[2903] The Defence Committee's view is that well-established strategic and operational cooperation between the state and the business community is needed to maintain this infrastructure

[2904] Few actors are completely independent in the emergency preparedness sector, which means that private-public collaboration is crucial

[2905] All stakeholders involved, including authorities, operators and subcontractors, as well as critical users who depend on electronic communications, need to work proactively to be able to maintain critical operations during times of heightened alert and, in the extreme, war

[2906] The lessons learned from Ukraine show the importance of systematic cybersecurity work, access to redundant and diversified communication routes, high robustness in the central systems of electronic communication networks, and well-functioning cooperation between private and public actors

[2907] The Government assesses that both the preparedness work of actors within the sector and the responsibilities between public and private actors need to be strengthened in order to meet the requirements during a heightened state of preparedness

[2908] This involves, for example, having the ability to exchange sensitive information during high alert, being able to maintain sustained repair readiness, and strengthening the ability of relevant actors in the sector to implement effective collaboration under difficult conditions

[2909] The Government, like the Defence Committee, is of the opinion that measures need to be taken to strengthen robustness and resilience in networks and services with the aim of strengthening resilience against both physical stresses and in the cyber domain

[2910] This may, for example, involve investments in reserve power to achieve sustainability in densely populated areas and areas of particular importance for total defense

[2911] The Government also believes that measures should be taken to increase redundancy and maintain functionality in critical parts of the networks and at alternative management locations

[2912] Robustness and redundancy are also needed in protected facilities of importance to maintain the ability for regional, national, and international communication in both everyday life and crisis as well as during heightened alert and extreme war

[2913] This requires continued government investment in infrastructure and for all stakeholders involved to prioritize work on resilience and preparedness

[2914] The Defence Committee's view is that systems for electronic communication and mail used in everyday life will be of great importance to all sectors of total defence, even during periods of heightened alert and in the event of war

[2915] Mobile networks are then expected to be of particular importance for the civilian population as well as the total defense

[2916] The distribution of mail and packages is vulnerable to power outages, sabotage, and disruptions in road and rail networks

[2917] Physical mail and parcel handling constitutes an important distribution channel for shipments of materials and supplies that cannot be conveyed electronically

[2918] The Government therefore believes that robustness-enhancing measures are also important for the postal sector

[2919] The Government further believes that it should be identified how the total defence's need for postal services is affected by increased readiness

[2920] In this work, experiences from Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine should be taken into account

[3274] The Government intends to return to the issue. Cybersecurity and cyber defence The Government's assessment

[3275] The systematic and risk-based work on information and cybersecurity should continue to be strengthened within all parts of total defense

[3276] The military's cyber defense capabilities, including the ability to conduct defensive and offensive cyber operations, should be further strengthened

[3277] The reasons for the government's assessment

[3278] The ability to handle cyber threats and cyber attacks is of fundamental importance to Sweden's security and resilience

[3279] This applies in peacetime, during high alert and in war

[3280] Basic protection against cyber threats is realized through systematic and risk-based information and cybersecurity work

[3281] In addition, cyber defense capabilities are required as part of military defense

[3282] The Defence Committee's view is that cybersecurity and cyber defence should be seen as mutually reinforcing activities

[3283] Threat image Various forms of antagonistic cyber activities are part of the normal picture today

[3284] The threat landscape against Sweden and Swedish interests is complex and includes, among other things, intelligence operations to steal, influence or destroy information or systems, cybercrime and so-called hacktivism, which is a form of data intrusion to promote political or social activism through espionage, sabotage, disinformation or blackmail

[3285] Foreign powers may be involved to varying degrees through actual implementation, control, support or tolerance of cyber attacks

[3286] The most serious cyber threats emanate primarily from the most qualified state or state-supported actors, primarily Russia, China and Iran

[3287] FRA, Must and the Swedish Security Service have found that cyberattacks carried out by qualified state and state-supported attackers against Sweden have increased in scope and capability

[3288] China conducts advanced cyber espionage to promote its own economic development and military capabilities

[3289] Russia is trying to obtain information about, for example, Swedish infrastructure, technology and information

[3290] The development and spread of commercial cyber capabilities means that more threat actors have access to qualified, offensive means

[3291] Several state actors have built up significant capabilities to be able to operate offensively in the cyber domain

[3292] Such attacks can complement political, diplomatic, economic, traditional kinetic military and other means, both individually during peacetime normal conditions and prior to or during all or part of a conflict, and threaten a nation's freedom of action and ultimately its sovereignty

[3293] According to NATO's 2022 Strategic Concept, one or more cyber activities could reach the level of armed attack and lead to the North Atlantic Council invoking Article 5 on collective defense

[3294] The 2020 Defense Decision (Government Bill 2020/21:30) stated that the effects of a cyber attack can have just as great consequences for vital societal functions and critical IT systems as a conventional armed attack, and thus in some cases can be considered an armed attack

[3295] The Defence Committee's view is that this assessment should continue to apply

[3296] Cybersecurity Information and cyber security as a prerequisite Sweden's security, competitiveness and prosperity rest largely on digital foundations

[3297] The Defence Committee notes that Sweden is a highly digitalized country

[3298] Our ability to harness and translate the extensive opportunities of digitalization into increased competitiveness and prosperity must go hand in hand with an equally good ability to manage the vulnerabilities that follow in its wake

[3299] Digitalization has made the cyberspace a prominent arena for threats and attacks against, for example, public institutions, companies and financial systems

[3300] Digitalization also entails complex chains of dependency where one actor's vulnerabilities can pose a risk to other actors

[3301] Attacks can have widespread effects

[3302] Cyber attacks in peacetime and during heightened alert and war can, simply put, aim to affect or destroy digital infrastructure and digital services within critical societal functions or to use these structures and services to carry out attacks against civilian objects and military targets within total defense operations

[3303] This implies that digital infrastructure and digital services must be so robust, redundant, secure, trusted and have such a high level of resilience that they function across the entire conflict scale, and that a good level of information and cybersecurity is a basic prerequisite for the entire total defense

[3304] It also follows from this that the actual effect of a cyber attack in a war situation is largely determined by how well prepared a country's relevant social actors are to resist and handle cyber attacks in peacetime

[3743] Defense Planning Process, NDPP

[3744] The goals have a high degree of concreteness and refer to both the number of combat units, their characteristics, mobility capabilities, interoperability, readiness and endurance, including, for example, the amount of ammunition

[3745] NATO's capability planning process also reviews and evaluates Allies' defence policies and plans, including financial plans, with particular emphasis on the implementation of NATO's capability goals

[3746] Every two years, a review is carried out that, among other things, compiles information on the Allies' national lists of military units and capabilities

[3747] While governance and monitoring of the Armed Forces will continue to take place through the governance forms applied in Swedish state administration, the government assesses that NATO membership will affect governance and monitoring within military defence in several respects

[3748] The need to have relevant data available at the right times for Swedish participation in NATO's capability planning process, for example, places new and changed requirements on data and reporting

[3749] Furthermore, joint decisions in NATO will need to be taken into account, which may lead to new or changed tasks for the authorities concerned

[3750] For effective and clear governance of military defense, (as well as civilian defense), and to 169 Prop

[3751] To ensure Swedish influence in the alliance, it is important that national processes for planning and follow-up relate to the joint planning in NATO

[3752] The Government intends to continue to maintain close dialogue with the relevant authorities

[3753] State property management in the defence sector

[3754] Within the infrastructure area, there is a need for the defense authorities to continue to develop collaboration, a holistic approach and coordination of operational plans, etc., in order to achieve growth and increased operational capability

[3755] The Fortifications Agency's operations are of great importance for growth in the defense sector in general

[3756] Investment levels in infrastructure for military defense will be high in the coming years, and the government believes that regulations and processes in the area need to be reviewed to ensure that growth can occur at the pace required to implement the decisions that the Riksdag and the government have made

[3757] It is of great importance that the management of the acquisition of infrastructure for total defence purposes keeps pace with the management of materiel acquisition and formation, and that the acquisition of infrastructure as a whole contributes to growth within military defence

[3758] Governance of civil defence. The government's assessment

[3759] The governance and monitoring of civil defence should be strengthened with the aim of promoting transparency and effectiveness and to create the conditions to strengthen civil defence capabilities and increase the pace of development

[3760] Civil defense should be governed from a holistic perspective with clear structures and processes for monitoring resources and results

[3761] Steering and monitoring should be based on the financial planning framework for civil defence for the defence decision period 2025–

[3762] The reasons for the government's assessment

[3763] Civil defense consists of a large number of actors and the resources for civil defense have increased significantly since reconstruction began in connection with the defense decision in 2015 (Government Bill

[3764] During the defense decision period to date, funds have been allocated at different times and to different parts of civil defense, both in the form of permanent and temporary funds

[3765] The funds allocated to the area have also partly had different purposes

[3766] This has included administrative costs associated with the authorities' ongoing civil defense activities, but also expenses that more directly strengthen civil defense capabilities in times of heightened alert and war

[3767] Examples of the latter include investments in equipment or control points

[3768] The fact that contributions have been made at different times and for different purposes has made it difficult to monitor how much funding has been allocated to each area within civil defense

[3769] It also contributes to a lack of clarity when it comes to understanding what type of activity is being funded and what results are being achieved

[3770] According to the government, inadequate follow-up means limitations in being able to effectively and efficiently prioritize efforts and steer towards Proposition

[3771] results in civil defense and thus achieve the increased ambitions in the area

[3772] Based on the financial planning framework for civil defence, the government therefore intends to strengthen governance and monitoring in the area

[3773] To achieve this, the government intends to review current structures and processes for governance and monitoring

[3774] The starting point in the work should be that the steering and monitoring is based on specified goals and from a holistic perspective that is based on central data and assessments of developments in the area

[3775] To achieve this, an important prerequisite is that the actors who receive funds from the financial planning framework for civil defence clearly account for how the funds have been used and what results have been achieved

[3776] According to the government, the overall purpose of such work is to ensure that the funds included in the civil defence financial planning framework are used to strengthen civil defence and thus to finance measures aimed at meeting the demands of heightened preparedness and, in the extreme, war

[3777] The Government believes that measures financed by funds from the civilian framework can ultimately also contribute to strengthening society's ability to prevent and manage difficult stresses in peace

[3778] In summary, the government believes that the governance and monitoring of civil defence should be strengthened with a particular focus on transparency and effectiveness, thereby achieving the increased level of ambition for civil defence that the global situation requires

[3779] Implementation

[3780] Against the backdrop of uncertainties in global developments, not least with regard to the continued development of Russia's war in Ukraine, there is an increased risk that the security situation could rapidly deteriorate further

[3781] The defense policy orientation presented in this bill may need to be adjusted based on changes in the security policy situation, but also based on Sweden's NATO membership and the associated demands on the war organization, including upcoming capability goals, as well as other external factors that affect the implementation of the defense decision

[3782] The reasons for the government's assessment

[3783] In this bill, the government proposes, among other things, the direction for the Swedish Armed Forces' war organization

[3784] The government also explains the direction that is necessary within civil defense

[3785] In addition, the government reports its assessment of important issues that will characterize the work within the various parts of total defense

[3786] The measures reported in the bill are justified based on the deteriorating security policy development and in particular Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Sweden's membership in NATO and the current state of military and civil defense where the need for measures has accumulated over a long time

[3787] Regardless of needs and ambitions, the Armed Forces and other authorities have reported a number of factors that constitute uncertainties and risks in the implementation of the measures reported in the bill, including those proposed by the Defence Committee

[3788] In some cases, these uncertainties and risks are significant

[3789] This applies to the starting point for the defense decision, the time for implementing various measures, estimated costs for these, and operational conditions outside the control of the authorities

[3790] The Government assesses that these are consequences that in various respects need to be taken into account when implementing the defense decision, but at the same time emphasizes that this does not reduce the need, suitability or urgency of the measures covered by this bill

[3791] The external situation and the current state of the Armed Forces thus justify a rapid increase in capabilities within military defense with the ambition reflected in this bill

[3792] At the same time, continued analysis and planning work will need to be carried out regarding the maintenance of major materiel systems, which may require reprioritization or other measures

[3793] As the government has previously stated, governance and monitoring need to be adapted to the capability increase that the defense will now undergo

[3794] Preparedness should be in place to adjust the direction based on developments in the world, Sweden's NATO membership and the associated demands on the war organization, including upcoming capability goals, as well as other external factors that affect the implementation of the defense decision

[3795] As stated above, the government also assesses that during the defense decision period, a renewed overall assessment of the construction of the security of supply may need to be made
